entry.title: Wild Like Me
entry.summary: "So, uh, let's play an old song. A really really old…
entry.content:
"So, uh, let's play an old song.

A really really old song.

Sing it loud, New York City.

This is called My Heart."

If I was an extravert (although I play one on the Internet), and I could sing (professionally; amateurly I'm hard to beat), I would like to step on stage and sing.

An old song.

One we hadn't played in years.

I don't have enough people who know me who can sing the words back to me, but I always love when the audience does so at concerts.

I mean, at some point I'm like, let the lead singer take back over.

But there are certain songs, like Phil Collins' live in Chicago album, where "Take Me Home" becomes an interactive event.

A choir of thousands.

And that kinda sheet just gives me goosebumps.

There's a live version of a Counting Crows song.

It's one of those where he interloops another completely unrelated song into one of their known songs.

And he sings, "She doesn't exist anymore..."

And you hear one guy, amongst the thousands, who screams this guttural "Yeaaaaah!!!"

It's so loud that the crowd erupts in an ovation.

And you know, love songs and heartbreak songs are like that.

It hit that guy so hard that the audience, even me listening on a iPod, could feel it.

In my home, we say every story is a love story.

But sometimes, it doesn't end well.

Heartbreaks.

Timelines.

Time.

But I don't know man.

Something about a love song is a beautiful, irreplaceable, thing.

But sometimes, the one that hits home, is when one guy screams "Yeah!!!" because he feels it in his burals.

There's something magical about music.

We could talk about vibration, frequency, and sonic energy.

But all I know is sometimes, even during the happiest times, a sad song is the best song.

Or at least, the right song.

"And trust me everything I am is yours."

"Just say the word."

...

"We keep the fire alive, through the trying times!" 

We're playing Aces high, but you're wild like me.

"YEEEEEEEEAAAAAAAAHHHHHHH!!!!"

🧨

Remember, no setbacks, no comebacks.

[Cue saxophone solo]

🎷

"And I wanna get to that place, I want lift up just a few feet off the ground, and see if we can't get a little close to the roof of this building."

🕴

entry.title: Alex In Wonderland
entry.summary: A lot of this is projection, you know. Communication. People say…
entry.content:
A lot of this is projection, you know.

Communication.

People say sheet to you they should be heeding.

It's got little to do with you, most of the time.

It's got more to do with the speaker.

And so I say this today to you.

There was some Navy Seal or something that wrote a book called No Easy Day.

And I really liked the title.

In a way that guys like tough titles.

Or implied ones.

And of course for a lot of us, there are easy days.

A lot of them.

And we tend to take them for granted.

But I've had a streak of hard days.

Not like Navy Seal hunting #1 target hard.

But hard for me.

Like "Is this going to be my life from here on?"

And while the answer sometimes is in fact yes.

A lot of times it's temporary.

The suck is temporary.

You just have to get through it.

Even though it feels like it's not going away.

Sometimes, hardest days feel permanent.

But I want you to believe it's not.

That it's going to get better.

You just have to get through the worst of it.

Believe it or not, it's made me a better person.

Or at least a more appreciative person.

If you have your health, you truly do have everything.

I wouldn't trade perfect health for my overall life as it is right now (does that make sense?), but I'd trade a lot for it.

You know that idea that the body completely regenerates new cells every six months?

That every six months, you're a new person?

Well, turns out that's not necessarily true.

Billions of cells renew every single day.

About 4 million cells every single second.

330 billion cells replaced every single day.

My wife's grandfather had this line that I just loved.

I'm in pretty good shape for the shape I'm in.

I think that now.

I hope to from here on out.

And if you're going through the opposite of an easy day right now.

I just have this to say.

Do whatever it takes to get through it.

Second by second.

Nanometer by nanometer.

My life hasn't been "normal" for ages.

And certainly not for the last half decade or so.

Good days seems so fleeting.

And hard days can seem so permanent.

But they're not.

Or at least they haven't been.

It's easier to say all this since I'm able to type.

But this is a game of willpower.

I didn't want this fight.

But sometimes, fights find me.

So here we go.

Another round.

In the rabbit hole.

🐇

entry.title: On A Bull Named Fu Manchu
entry.summary: I'm slowly catching up to the news I missed. And wowzers.
entry.content:
I'm slowly catching up to the news I missed.

And wowzers.

Lot going on out there.

Of course, I haven't really checked much of the news.

I just know that by saying wowzers and lot going on out there, it makes it seem so.

Instead, I'm grinding.

Trying to heal.

To pass the time without wasting it.

Anymore than I have.

Anymore than I already have.

One of my very best friends and people I'd ever known was quite a bit older than me.

And he'd spend all day bragging about his family.

Just how much he loved them.

How accomplished they were.

How beautiful, how handsome, how intelligent.

Now, we worked at a gym at the time, and he was technically my boss, but we still give him a lot of sheet for it.

He sadly passed far too soon.

But he's one of my favorite people who ever walked the earth.

Just a genuinely happy, decent, good man.

Who loved his family.

A little too much.

And I think, I think, that's the sweet spot.

We used to go shopping to get supplies and he'd stop me in the entry way. Right after you walk in but before the 2nd set of doors to actually be inside the store.

He'd pause.

Say hold on.

Then he'd start giggling.

And I smelled it.

Sometimes, he'd just start giggling in his truck, on our many road trips.

And I knew what that meant.

My Lord, do I miss that man.

💨

entry.title: I Love You
entry.summary: I don't really want you to know hard days. Yes, you…
entry.content:
I don't really want you to know hard days.

Yes, you do.

But yes, I do.

Do you want to know why?

Because an easy life is a wasted life.

I say this because I have had a blessed life.

And there were times of ease, even though it didn't seem easy at the time.

But it takes hard days to really show you how easy those days were.

How blessed you are.

I want you to have hard days you can bounce back from.

Stronger than ever.

I don't want you to have the kind you can't.

Recency bias is a heck of a thing.

The latest challenges feel like the hardest.

But in my truest frame I know that simply isn't so.

It's just here right now.

And let me say, it was terrible.

I don't want to rank terribles, but it was right up there.

Right now, it's kinda bad.

Which I'll take.

Kinda bad leads to kinda ok which leads to kinda good.

This most recent kinda good day was trending to really good, then whammo!

Went really south.

It's all really strange, but I want to write about it as contemporaneously (and vaguely) as I can.

And the fact that I can write at all shows that I'm doing well enough to do that.

At the end of the day, this whole place is a love letter to my family.

To my wife.

To my children.

To my blood.

Daddy going through it right now.

But Daddy been through it before.

And each time.

Every time.

Daddy had something to fight for.

Had someones to fight for.

And you'll never know how much that fuels me.

I'd try to tell you here, but I'd be a faucet.

I'm a lifelong loner who turned into a family man.

Thanks to you.

Ordeals are stern teachers.

But remember, this, too, shall pass.

I love you.

And I thank you.

For giving me something and someones to live for.

Thank you, God.

For the reminders.

entry.title: Raised Dots
entry.summary: This is a mental game. What? Life. Oh. Sure, there's lots…
entry.content:
This is a mental game.

What?

Life.

Oh.

Sure, there's lots of physical.

But the game is mental.

And therefore, spiritual, too.

One of my heroes is the late great Charlie Munger.

He really isn't known for much besides make a lot of money.

But this is a true disservice to his life.

Because what I love about him is just how tough he was.

He went through horrific events.

Yeah, even billionaires have tragedy.

And while I won't mention his gravest, I will share one.

Charlie loved to read.

Voracious.

I believe he enjoyed it more than making money (which he enjoyed a lot).

And there was a time in his life where he believed he was going to lose sight in his last working eye.

For you see, he had been half-blind for years.

Already down to 50%.

And for a lover of reading, this didn't get Charlie down.

He kept reading with his one good eye.

And then, later in his life, there was a realistic chance that he was losing the vision in his good eye.

So what did he do?

Mope about it?

Cry about it?

Call it a life?

Oh no.

Not Mr. Munger.

Instead, he learned braille.

So he could continue to read.

Even if he couldn't see the words.

He would learn to feel them.

Touch them.

Like goose bumps.

He wouldn't give up one of his favorite things to do.

📗

Simply because he couldn't see the words.

Instead, he would learn to feel them.

As a young man, I measured toughness by how many villains you could slay.

And how unscathed you'd be after it all.

But the reality is, that's not toughness.

I mean it is, but work with me here.

Toughness is being told, "Hey, you're already half blind, but your other eye is going, too."

And after a period of processing, you get to work.

You bounce back and learn to read with your other senses.

I'd probably go audiobooks.

I prefer them now anyways.

But my ears are starting to go.

My eyes aren't the greatest either.

Part of the long term effects of surviving what I am surviving.

Thank you, God.

We all like to think toughness looks like muscular headbanded mullets holding a machine gun in each hand.

Or maybe just me as an 80s kid.

But really, true toughness looks like everyone else.

Can be in everyone else.

Like inside you and inside me.

Sometimes in an old man in a nice suit, just shuffling through his favorite books.

Another kind of unstoppable.

Rest in peace, Charlie.

Hope you know, now.

👼

entry.title: Teacher Called Humble Pie
entry.summary: I wish I could convince you how lucky you are. To…
entry.content:
I wish I could convince you how lucky you are.

To be on the ground floor of the Maslow heirarchy.

Or at least, to have that floor satisfied.

Air to breathe.

Water to drink.

Food to eat.

Roof over head.

The ability to get a good night's sleep.

There's a line that goes "If you don't have your health, you don't have anything."

And that line has been on my mind of late.

I'm able to write, perhaps not nearly at my best (such as it was), but here I sits and types.

How lucky.

If I could, I would tell you more.

But privacy is privacy for a reason.

On the days and times I feel well enough, I will muster up a musing.

But until then, remember this:

What good is hitting the pinnacle of Actualization if you're struggling on the first floor?

So today's lesson is, to have everything, you have to first have your health.

First principles.

Life teaches the greatest lessons.

And I am learning every single second.

entry.title: Tungsten
entry.summary: Put your money where your mouth is. We all have heard…
entry.content:
Put your money where your mouth is.

We all have heard of that.

It means, back up your words with actions, hard work, and even dinero.

Well, I got something that might be more helpful.

Put your faith where your mouth is.

It's easy to have faith when things are going well, although we sometimes take it for granted.

But when things get tough (and they will, over and over, if you live long enough), when you have to back your faith up with actions, hard work, and yes even dinero, your faith is then truly tested.

Praising God is easy when things are going well.

When you're clearly blessed.

Healthy.

Loved.

Iterating to Actualization.

The truth is, even with all my trials and tribulations, I haven't gone through nearly the level of stuff some of you have. Or will.

Even this current T & T pales in comparison to some of your tests, past, present and future.

I wish I could protect you from all of it, but I can't.

And I think it'd do you a disservice.

Complacency and ruts come from comfort sometimes.

And I never want you to feel that way.

Contentment and peace, yes.

Grace is amazing.

Do you understand that?

I hope you do.

I know I do.

A couple weeks ago, the last thing I cared about was writing on this thing.

And I must admit, it's no longer a "must do".

But I just want to share, fights for yourself come on a lot of levels.

And I hope, I pray, you fight till the glorious end.

And remember, sometimes getting better is like the stock market.

Up, down, up, way down, up, way up, wayyyyyyyyy up.

You get the idea.

It's easy to see what you're made of when things are easy.

So what are you made of when things get hard?

entry.title: All Of This Is A Love Letter
entry.summary: When you get a note from your child that starts with…
entry.content:
When you get a note from your child that starts with "To the best daddy in the world," well it's enough to make a grown man cry.

I don't share this to brag.

At least about myself.

I'm not the best daddy in the world.

I'm sure there's one or two better.

I brag because of the heart of my children.

Of my family.

As a former loner, I never used to NEED anyone.

But I see that's no longer true.

If it ever was.

Praise God.

I need help.

From the people I love.

To do what they've always done since day one.

Take care of me.

As I have them.

An imperfect circle.

But one my mind has to come to grips with.

And not feel so ashamed about.

Let them help me.

Feel emboldened and empowered by their help.

And so that's the lesson for today.

Help others help you.

Love,

The luckiest daddy in the world (I am willing to share this title, dads).

entry.title: Instant Healing, Over Time
entry.summary: I'd like to think I'm tough. But I'm not. I'm not…
entry.content:
I'd like to think I'm tough.

But I'm not.

I'm not tough.

Yes, you are.

At least when compared to my loved ones.

Oh, sure.

Who have had to take care of me for so many years.

And have to do so again.

My children have stepped up and taken everything in stride.

Tough times make for tough people.

But no one's been stronger, is stronger, than my wife.

She's been with me through sickness and in health.

For richer and poorer.

And she's trying her best to get me to health.

As a man, it both crushes and strengthens me that she is working so diligently to keep everything as normal as possible considering the circumstances.

And they are kinda strange circumstances.

But such is my life.

So much of life requires physical toughness.

But so much more important is mental toughness.

Spiritual toughness.

So the thing I'd say is God is giving me the grace to write a little again, which implies so much beyond just the surface benefit.

I couldn't write for weeks.

Didn't even want to if I could.

And with my few words here I want to advise you to work on your mental and spiritual toughness.

And silver lining wise, that really can only happen when you're in the sheet.

A silver lining to the sheet.

So here we go again.

Day by day.

Hour by hour.

Inch by inch.

Let's see what I'm made of.

entry.summary: Crazy times. Going through something. I'd say more but I don't…
entry.content:
Crazy times. 

Going through something.

I'd say more but I don't want to.

Just weird stuff.

Albeit a bit more wobbly.

Thank you, God. 

I know you're teaching me something.
